title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp.194-196). This page belongs to Grothendieck's notes on what is now the Grothendieck–Katz p-curvature conjecture. On p.194 he takes a smooth X→S, with S of finite type and dominant over Z and generic point y, and a module with connection E. He asks: if E_s has zero p-curvature for all closed s of characteristic p>0, is E_y integrable, i.e. does it have finite monodromy?

For rank 1 he splits the question in two:
- (a) is the class of E_y in Pic(X_y) torsion?
- (b) if a closed 1-form ω has every reduction ω_s locally logarithmic (detected by the Cartier operator, C̃ω_s = ω_s), is some integer multiple of ω_y logarithmic?

On p.196, for an abelian scheme, he translates this through the universal vector extension E of the dual abelian scheme A. The translation is question (c): if a section ω of E satisfies ω(s) ∈ pE_s for all closed s, is its image in A torsion? He then generalises to question (d). Let S be integral, of finite type and dominant over Spec Z, E a group scheme of finite type over S, and ω ∈ E(S). Suppose that for every closed s, ω(s) lies in a subgroup of E_s which is connected and either proper / of unipotent rank zero / affine / unipotent. Does ω(y) then lie in a subgroup of E_y of the same type?

The present page (p.195) continues (d) and should begin "(resp. de rang unipotent nul, resp. affine, resp. unipotent)".
- NB: the cases 'connected affine' and 'unipotent' are said to be trivial, via Chevalley's structure theorem for algebraic groups.
- In the unipotent case the hypothesis amounts to ω(s) being killed by p^N, with p = char k(s) and N bounded in terms of the dimension.
- When E is commutative, the 'unipotent rank zero' case is reformulated as follows. Suppose there is an N such that for all closed s, ω(s) ∈ (p^N E)(s) = p^N E(s), i.e. ω(s) is divisible by p^N in E_s. Then one wants ω(y) to lie in a subgroup of E_y of unipotent rank zero, i.e. an extension of an abelian variety by a torus.
- This makes sense because for N large, multiplication by p^N kills the unipotent part of a connected commutative group in characteristic p. Its image is therefore semi-abelian, so divisibility by p^N is the natural characteristic-p shadow of 'lying in a semi-abelian subgroup'.
- If this were known, the 'connected proper' case would reduce to E already being an extension of an abelian variety A by a torus T. That is a semi-abelian variety, where one must then show that ω(y) lies in an abelian subvariety.
- A crossed-out passage starts the semi-abelian case: if the torus part is non-trivial, one needs some independence or indivisibility argument.
- The oblique marginal note says one may assume E_y has unipotent rank zero, hence is an extension of an abelian variety by a torus. One then needs a criterion of 'indivisibility' to exclude a nonzero toric component.
- The page ends on characteristic p > 0 and an exclamation.

The page is a sequence of reductions of a local–global question for points of group schemes: properties of reductions at all closed points should propagate to the generic fibre.
errors: Over finite residue fields every point lies in a finite (hence proper) subgroup. The hypothesis in (d) is only meaningful with the word 'connexe', which Grothendieck indeed added on p.196. The page's arguments implicitly rely on it.

Calling the affine and unipotent cases 'trivial' via Chevalley is plausible but not argued. In characteristic 0, ω(y) must be shown to lie in the linear part, and in the unipotent case to be a unipotent element. This needs passing from closed points to the generic point, e.g. via constructibility of the locus where the class in the abelian quotient vanishes. That step is not written out.

The equality (p^N E)(s) = p^N E(s) mixes the image subgroup scheme with groups of points. Over a finite field these differ by the cokernel of p^N on rational points. One should use points over an algebraic closure or the scheme-theoretic image.

ideas.what: Reduction of the rank-one p-curvature conjecture (via the universal vector extension of the dual abelian scheme) to a local–global question on sections of group schemes over a base of finite type over Z.
ideas.modern_name: Rank-one case of the Grothendieck–Katz p-curvature conjecture; universal vector extension A^♮
ideas.usually_credited_to: N. Katz (Invent. Math. 1972, 'Algebraic solutions of differential equations'), later work by the Chudnovskys, Y. André, J.-B. Bost
ideas.where_published: Not in Grothendieck's own publications; the conjecture is attributed to him in Katz 1972

ideas.what: Question (d) in its 'unipotent rank zero' form: if ω(s) is divisible by p^N in E_s at every closed s, then ω(y) lies in a semi-abelian subgroup of E_y.
ideas.modern_name: Local–global principle for subgroups / detecting membership or linear dependence by reduction maps
ideas.usually_credited_to: Related later work: Corrales-Rodrigáñez–Schoof (support problem, 1997), Larsen, Pink (2004), Perucca (2008-10)

ideas.what: Using Chevalley's structure theorem (linear part, abelian quotient, unipotent radical) to split the question into affine / unipotent / unipotent-rank-zero / proper cases.
ideas.modern_name: Chevalley structure theorem; dévissage of commutative algebraic groups

ideas.what: In characteristic p, multiplication by p^N kills the unipotent part of a connected commutative group, so divisibility by p^N detects semi-abelian subgroups.
ideas.modern_name: Structure of commutative algebraic groups in characteristic p

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates a general local–global question for arbitrary group schemes of finite type over a base of finite type over Z, in four variants (proper, unipotent rank 0, affine, unipotent). He reduces the proper case to the semi-abelian case, conditional on a divisibility statement, and leaves the semi-abelian 'indivisibility' step open. As far as I know, this general formulation, especially the criterion 'divisible by p^N at all closed points ⇒ generic point lies in a semi-abelian subgroup', is not stated in the literature in this generality.
missed.quote: supposons qu'il existe un entier N tel que ... (p^N E)(s) = (p^N E_s)(s) = p^N E(s), i.e. qu'il soit divisible par p^N
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It anticipates the reduction-map / support-problem literature (Pink, Larsen, Perucca) and frames the rank-one p-curvature conjecture as one instance of a uniform local–global principle for group schemes. That framing could guide attacks on the remaining cases.

missed.claim: An explicit link between Cartier-operator criteria for logarithmic forms, divisibility of points of the universal vector extension, and Chevalley-type dévissage of algebraic groups, all in service of the p-curvature conjecture.
missed.quote: se ramènerait au cas où E est déjà une extension d'une V.A. A par un tore T
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It connects the Grothendieck–Katz conjecture with arithmetic questions on reductions of points in semi-abelian varieties, an area developed independently later.

deep.surprise_reason: The abelian-variety reformulation of the rank-one case is known through Katz (1972). The general group-scheme local–global question (d) and its reduction via divisibility are a notable unpublished detail anticipating later reduction-map work, but they are left as open questions.

'NB Les cas "affine" {connexe}, "unipotent" sont triviaux' — the superscript is 'connexe', not 'convexe'.
'rep. unipotent unel' throughout should be 'rang unipotent nul'.
'd'un VA par un tore' should be 'extension d'une V.A. par un tore'.
Unipotent case likely reads: 'l'hypothèse signifie que ω(s) est annulé par p^N (p = car k(s))'.
